analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/hardware-support.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a 10-line paragraph (head 1085-1094 per changed_ranges) on the serial-prefill Gemma 4 pipeline default width. The paragraph says it adds no load-time allocation, that the paged pool capacity is a ceiling with pages reserved per request (CBv2StageKVHost), that each lane is charged its whole request state on every rank and admitted against live memory (QwenResidentRuntime.reserveLane), that a lane the host cannot hold is refused alone and retryably, and that the measured activation floor still applies. I examined this against the threat model, in particular T-029 (GPU resource availability), TB-007 (inference engine) and T-041 (prefix cache). It is documentation only. No code, control, endpoint, key handling, attestation path, authorization boundary or cache policy changes, so I found no security regression and no invalidated assumption.

The head text I was given is truncated at line 447, and the base excerpt starts at 878. I therefore saw the new paragraph only through the patch excerpt, not as numbered head lines. The excerpt is marked complete, so I did not treat the gap as evidence of a problem.

The claims in the new paragraph are not verifiable from the supplied evidence: that the width default adds no load-time allocation, that reservations are refused per lane, and that the activation floor still applies. They rest on code outside this PR (DistributedInstalledPlan.gemma4PipelineBatchLanes, CBv2StageKVHost, QwenResidentRuntime.reserveLane). If the corresponding code change lands separately, the next pass should check that admission against live memory is actually enforced per lane, since a missing check there would be an availability risk (T-029, T-016). That is a question for the code change, not a finding here.
